challenge.method: For each edition, I compared the full publisher body with its decoded SPDX licenseText first verbatim and then after replacing only typographic double quotation marks in the publisher body. I also compared each normalized body with the opposite edition’s licenseText and inspected the names, headings, first redistribution condition, and notice placeholders.
challenge.results: For both 1.0 and 1.1, verbatim equality was false, normalized same-edition equality was true, and normalized cross-edition equality was false. The quote differences occur around “Asset Name” and “AS IS”. Edition 1.1 has the SPDX name `ASWF Digital Assets License 1.1` and adds a clause requiring a description, if applicable, of how redistributed assets differ from the originals. Edition 1.0 ends that condition after the disclaimer reference. These differences rule out an edition merge.

limitations: The correspondence covers the specified SPDX detail and foundation template. Both contain literal <Asset Name>, <Year>, and <Asset Owner> placeholders. Establishing the license for an individual asset requires its own license notice.

SPDX cites the foundation file on the moving main branch. The reviewed comparison uses the foundation commit and content digest in the acquisition record. The shared text supplies no independent corroboration of licensing for any work.
The SPDX tag is unsigned. Its repository record establishes the documented release-to-commit mapping without authenticating the tagger by signature.
reasoning: At the commit identified by the SPDX v3.29.0 tag, the detail record pairs licenseId `ASWF-Digital-Assets-1.0` with the exact name `ASWF Digital Assets License version 1.0`. Its decoded licenseText matches the entire pinned Academy Software Foundation v1.0 template after replacing U+201C and U+201D with U+0022. This includes the placeholders and final newline.
